newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUG 12.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has proclaimed that Australia are currently the world's best cricket team after celebrating their fifth-Test victory ,and Australia's fifth successive Ashes series win. Page 1.

19 year-old Michael Klim has become Australia's fastest swimmer ever after last night winning the 100m freestyle at the Pan Pacific championships in Fukuoka, Japan. Matt Dunn came first in the 400m individual medley, and Samantha Riley won the 100m breasroke. The overnight successes have given Australia three gold medals for the second consecutive night. Page 18.

Wallaby skipper John Eales may not play in Saturday's rugby Tri-Nations Test against New Zealand due to a damaged medial ligament in his left knee. A decision will be made later this morning as to Eales' condition, and Saturday's starting lineup. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian women's soccer team has maintained a three-match unbeaten record after wins against Hungary and Sweden, and a draw against Budapest. On its tour of Europe, the Australian team beat Hungary 4-0, and is due to play the Netherlands in Amsterdam on Thursday. Page 44.

New South Wales surfer Beau Emerton has become the first surfer this year to beat four-time world champion Kelly Slater. Emerton rode four mandatory scoring waves against Slater's seven at Huntington Beach in California, totally 28.93 points to Slater's 28.16. Page 44.

Queensland javelin thrower Joanna Stone was the world's female best at the World Athletics Championships in Athens on Saturday, becoming one of four Australian medallists at the championships. Steve Moneghetti scored a bronze medal as final proof of his standing as a marathoner. Page 44.
THE AGE

Australian Football League West Coast Eagles chief executive Brian Cook has proposed a veteran's allowance to AFL officials. The allowance means a club can maintain the contracts of older players at current levels or offer them more money to stay. Page 6.
Australian soccer defender Jason Van Blerk has joined the England first division soccer club Manchester City on a free transfer from second division Millwall. PageB7.

The Moonee Valley Race Course is surprised at the lack of entries for next Saturday's Mitchell McKenzie Stakes. Receiving only three entries, assistant racing manager Vin Lowe says he could not recall a smaller entry for a black-type race at the Valley. Due to limited entries, the club has extended entries until 10am today for all races except the Manikato Stakes. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Football League Tribunal has cleared North Melbourne captain Wayne Carey of a tripping charge against Brisbane player Craig McRae in the second quarter at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Friday night. Page 72.
AFL Geelong player Grant Tanner has a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and is not expected to play again until 1999. Tanner is due for surgery this week. Page 70.

National Basketball Association Indiana Pacers coach Larry Bird is likely to receive a favourable report on Australian under-23 captain Sam Mackinnon, after two scouts for the Pacers were seen to express a considerable interest in the player at the world championships in Melbourne. Page 64.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australia has secured third place at baseball's Intercontinental Cup in Barcelona. The Australian team won bronze after beating the United States 7-6. Australia also beat the US in the round-robin section last week for the first time ever in a baseball ournament. Page 62.

Rugby Union players David Wilson and Jason Little have been named as candidates to replace Australian Wallabies captain John Eales in the match against New Zealand in the Tri-Nations rugby test in Dunedin on Saturday. The final decision, waiting to be mae later this week, comes as Eales is almost certainly out after a training accident yesterday. Page 62.

Australian Super League Brisbane Broncos player Shane Walker has been ruled out of the Super League and World Club Challenge finals due to a knee injury. Walker is due to undergo knee construction surgery. Page 58.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
